processing_steps.method: casting in a vacuum induction furnace
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The alloyed steel was produced by casting using a 100 kW vacuum induction furnace, resulting in 0.5 kg ingots (Table 1).
The ingots were hot-rolled at 1150 °C, obtaining 5 mm flat products, followed by water quenching; this is the parent process of the 800 °C tempering.

Samples were heat treated at 800 °C for 30 min, followed by water quenching. Tempering at 800 °C triggered complete and widespread transformations such as cellular transformation coupled with spinodal decomposition; for 12Al-30Mn-1C the austenite grains were fully spinodally decomposed.

structures.overall_structure: At 800 °C the austenite (γ) grains of 12Al-30Mn-1C were fully spinodally decomposed. Optical microscopy shows strongly contrasted light and dark grains, several showing internal transformation/banding; SEM shows rounded, droplet-like light regions in a darker matrix, consistent with spinodal decomposition. Nano-sized κ-carbides form as agglomerated acicular-like precipitates, the finest and least dense configuration among the three spinodally decomposed alloys examined.

phases_present.crystal_structure: FCC (austenite); spinodal pathway γ → γ0 + γ' → γ0 + L12 → γ0 + L12/E21
phases_present.morphology: roughened spinodally decomposed matrix with rounded droplet-like light regions in a darker matrix; optical contrast shows strongly contrasted light and dark grains with internal transformation

phases_present.crystal_structure: ordered (L12 initially, further ordering of C to E21 / L12)
phases_present.morphology: agglomerated into acicular-like (needle-like) precipitates; finest and least dense network among the three spinodally decomposed alloys

precipitates.distribution: agglomerated acicular-like precipitates forming a fine, less dense network; in the ×10,000 view they surround large bright blocky islands
precipitates.coherency: coherent with γ (coherency strain energy between κ-carbides and γ is essential for γ decomposition by spinodal decomposition)

phase_interfaces.coherence: coherent; the coherency strain energy between κ-carbides and γ is reported as essential for γ decomposition, and spinodal decomposition generates intragranular nano-sized cube-shaped κ-carbides within the γ phase

interfaces.phase_evolution: γ → γ0 + γ' → γ0 + L12 → γ0 + L12/E21 spinodal decomposition pathway. At 800 °C for 12Al-30Mn-1C the spinodal decomposition involved the entire austenitic volume (Fig. 13(c)); high Mn raises austenite stability so spinodal decomposition becomes more significant and occurs at the expense of cellular transformation.
interfaces.interface_notes: No specific δ-ferrite/γ interfaces or grain-boundary carbide films are reported for this particular composition; δ/γ carbide precipitation features reported elsewhere belong to other alloys (e.g. 12Al-10Mn-1C, 9Al-20/30Mn-1C).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers macro-hardness; 5 kg load applied for all indentations; 5 indentations per sample; measured on the 800 °C — tempered state of 12Al-30Mn-1C

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Vickers hardness: hot-rolled 324 HV vs 800 °C tempered 352 HV for 12Al-30Mn1C (Table 5); the 800 °C tempering gave a modest increase in hardness, unlike the strong hardening seen for other compositions

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Through-thickness embedding, grinding and polishing performed separately for hot-rolled and heat-treated samples
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyse the microstructure of the 800 °C tempered alloys
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 800 °C tempered 12Al-30Mn-1C optical micrograph shows strongly contrasted light and dark grains, several with internal transformation/banding.

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning Electron Microscopy (Secondary Electron Imaging, SEI)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Secondary electron images acquired to analyse phase morphologies; performed only on selected microstructures
characterization_methods.purpose: Resolve the microstructure/phase morphology of the 800 °C tempered 12Al-30Mn-1C
characterization_methods.key_findings: SEM shows rounded droplet-like light regions in a darker matrix consistent with spinodal decomposition (Fig. 5(d)); at higher magnification the spinodal nano-sized κ-carbides appear as agglomerated acicular-like precipitates, the finest and least dense configuration (Fig. 8(e,f)).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EDX-spectroscopy to provide qualitative information on local phase composition
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyse local phase chemical composition (Al, Mn partitioning)
characterization_methods.key_findings: EDS was performed on selected microstructures; no dedicated EDS table is reported for the 800 °C tempered 12Al-30Mn-1C composition (EDS tables given for 9Al-10Mn-1C and 12Al-20Mn-1C).

characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify hardening effects of the transformations

characterization_methods.technique: CALPHAD thermodynamic phase-fraction (phase volume fraction) diagrams
characterization_methods.purpose: Assess thermodynamic gradients for austenite stability vs tempering temperature
characterization_methods.key_findings: For 12Al-30Mn-1C (Fig. 12(d)) a BCC_2SL curve plateaus near 0.80 mol between ~400 and 600 °C then declines; KAPPA_E21 sits near 0.20 mol up to ~300 °C; FCC_A1 near 0.72 mol at ~1000 °C. The higher Al moves the f.c.c. field to higher temperatures, affecting austenite stability and justifying the γ propensity to transform.

computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD equilibrium thermodynamic calculation (phase amounts vs temperature)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase fractions (Amount of all phases, mol, 0.00–1.10) calculated over 0–1300 °C for composition 12Al-30Mn-1C. Legend phases: BCC_2SL, FCC_A1, LIQUID, KAPPA_E21, BCC_A2. BCC_2SL rises to a ~0.80 mol plateau between roughly 400 and 600 °C then declines; KAPPA_E21 sits near 0.20 mol up to ~300 °C then decreases; FCC_A1 near 0.72 mol at ~1000 °C.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Used to explain the reversal in austenite stability (higher Al moves the f.c.c. field toward higher temperatures, away from the tempering temperature) that justifies the propensity of the γ phase to transform by spinodal decomposition at 800 °C.

analytical_models.equation_role: Equilibrium phase amounts vs temperature used to infer thermodynamic gradients for austenite stability
analytical_models.model_note: No numeric data labels are printed on the curves; values are read from the figure description.

unmapped_findings: For 12Al-30Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C, only spinodal decomposition involved the entire austenitic volume (Fig. 13(c)); high manganese raised austenite stability so spinodal decomposition became more significant and occurred at the expense of cellular transformation (block b0110, b0113).

Hardness comparison for 12Al-30Mn1C (Table 5): hot-rolled 324 HV → 800 °C tempered 352 HV; in the discussion the paper notes that thickening of precipitates/low inter-lamellar spacing behaviour means some 800 °C tempered structures kept hardness close to their hot-rolled value rather than being strongly strengthened (blocks b0043, b0048, b0051, b0108).

The conclusions text (block b0122) attributes to 'the chemical composition featuring 12% Al + 30% Mn' the 'most dense and thickest nano-sized cuboidal κ-carbides' combined with 'spinodal decomposition + cellular transformation', which contradicts both Fig. 8(e,f)/the results text (12Al-30Mn-1C = finest, least dense acicular-like κ-carbides, and full spinodal decomposition without cellular transformation) and block b0121 (which attributes the medium-dense thin needle-like κ-carbides to 12% Al + 20% Mn). This internal inconsistency is noted here; the results-section description was used for the structure fields.

Fig. 8(e,f) for 12Al-30Mn-1C at 800 °C (×10,000 and ×30,000) shows agglomerated acicular precipitates surrounding large bright blocky islands, appearing as the finest and least dense acicular carbide network of the three alloys (blocks b0058, b0066).
